articles.title: KALSHI HALTS UTAH OPERATIONS WHILE AVOIDING IMMEDIATE BAN IN NEW YORK
articles.summary: Kalshi paused operations in Utah, where it had 177,000 users, after a federal judge let the state enforce its gambling laws. It is waiting on a ruling on the CFTC's request to block Utah from enforcing against it. In New York, Justice Melissa Crane denied the Attorney General's request for a temporary restraining order, saying the questions around derivatives and preemption are complex. Kalshi had warned the order could shut it down nationwide. The CFTC and DOJ have also sued Utah, Arkansas, Louisiana, and New York over state enforcement against prediction markets.

articles.title: CFTC STAFF ADVISORY PERMITS CRYPTO ASSETS TO COUNT TOWARD FINANCIAL RESOURCES REQUIREMENTS
articles.summary: The CFTC issued a staff advisory on permitting derivatives trading platforms and clearinghouses to count bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins toward the one-year operating cost coverage component of their financial resources requirements. Firms must still hold cash or highly liquid securities to satisfy a separate liquidity requirement, so crypto assets cannot fully replace traditional capital reserves under the framework. Prior CFTC rules were silent on whether crypto counted toward the operating cost threshold, leaving registered entities without clear guidance on how to treat native asset holdings on their balance sheets. The advisory, issued under Chairman Mike Selig, reflects the CFTC's approach of using staff guidance to extend crypto clarity in derivatives markets without full rulemaking cycles.

articles.title: ETHEREUM FOUNDATION DOUBLES SECURITY TEAM FOR POST-QUANTUM OVERHAUL
articles.summary: The Ethereum Foundation's first PQAI post says AI has become a more urgent risk than quantum computing, with models finding bugs in production software faster than people can review them, and the EF has doubled its protocol security team in response. After more than a year evaluating signature schemes, the EF is advocating hash-based cryptography to replace elliptic curves in three places: hash-based validator keys for consensus, a migration path to hash-based signatures for wallets, and hash-based blob commitments. Justin Drake put forward December 2028 as a target at Devcon, with 2029 as the EF's internal deadline and a timeline review in January, while Ethlabs pulled its Quick Slots proposal out of Hegotá to free up engineering time. The EF calls the upgrade harder than the Merge and warns that BLS tooling, pre-quantum contracts, wallets, multisigs, and staking pools all need changes.

articles.title: CROSS RIVER BANK ENTERS BITCOIN-BACKED LENDING WITH $250K LOANS
articles.summary: Cross River Bank and LendingUSA launched a Bitcoin-backed lending program on November 23, offering loans from $10,000 to $250,000 with LTV options at 30%, 50%, or 70% of collateral value. Borrowers can make interest-only payments or defer until maturity, though a BTC price decline triggers additional collateral requirements and potential liquidation of pledged holdings custodied by a qualified third party. This marks Cross River's first entry as a Bitcoin loan originator, adding FDIC-insured bank competition to an existing market that includes Ledn, Coinbase through Morpho, Column N.A. via Strike, and Fortis Bank through Unchained.

articles.title: BINANCE HIRES PLATFORMS FOR INDEPENDENT SECURITY REVIEWS
articles.summary: Binance engaged Google Cloud's Mandiant, blockchain security firm SlowMist, and Verichains to run comprehensive, independent reviews of its security procedures, validating current infrastructure and assessing its security posture going forward. CSO Jimmy Su said Binance is committed to acting on what the firms find, and co-CEO Richard Teng called user asset security the exchange's "first responsibility." The announcement covers only the engagement, with no published scope, completion date, or commitment to release findings. It comes 25 days after the intrusion on October 29 that took more than $6 billion and that the DOJ attributes to North Korean actors, which the release does not mention.

articles.title: UK BARS CRYPTO EXCHANGES FROM MARKET MAKING ON THEIR OWN PLATFORMS
articles.summary: HM Treasury made S.I. 2026/1219 on November 18, adding Article 9UA, which excludes dealing as a market maker on a qualifying cryptoasset trading platform (QCATP) from the regulated activity of dealing in qualifying cryptoassets as principal. The FCA's final rule CRYPTO 6.6.1R bars a QCATP operator from executing orders against its proprietary capital on the platform it runs, and guidance CRYPTO 6.6.4G states the operator cannot act as a market maker there. Operators can still use matched principal trading for client orders under non-discretionary rules and deal as principal away from their own venue, but must identify, monitor, and disclose market makers and any liquidity incentive schemes. The rules take effect with the UK's new crypto regime on October 25, 2027.

articles.title: MONAD'S FIRST YEAR: WHAT THE TEAMS HAVE BUILT SINCE MAINNET
articles.summary: A one-year anniversary article crediting the teams behind Monad. Consensus work progressed from MonadBFT to Cadence, with Quantum Cadence making safety independent of signatures. Other work includes BTX threshold encryption for an encrypted mempool, APES ordering preferences, a zkVM, Private Settlement Domains, MIP-8 page-aware storage pricing, and passkey-derived accounts. Ecosystem figures: 885 teams in the Metropolis hackathon and $82M of weekly tokenized equities volume, up 90% week over week. Visa added Monad to its stablecoin settlement program, Rain supports cards on it, and MetaMask runs its Money Account earn and card program there.

articles.title: STELLAR'S BELL (PROTOCOL 30) BRINGS SMART ACCOUNTS AND QUANTUM-SAFE SIGNATURES
articles.summary: Stellar's Protocol 30 upgrade, Bell, is live on mainnet following the validator vote on November 23. CAP-84 adds muxed contract addresses, a new "W" format carrying a 64-bit ID, so one smart account can hold funds for many customers in an omnibus model instead of one contract per customer, and CAP-87 lets smart contracts verify NIST's ML-DSA post-quantum signatures natively inside Stellar Core. CAP-88 moves ledger close times to a millisecond clock, removing the one-second floor so future upgrades can push block times below the current 5 seconds. Network transaction signatures stay Ed25519, and indexers or explorers that decode raw ledger data must update their XDR definitions because the ledger header format changes.

articles.title: ONDO USES OPEN USD FOR INSTANT USDY SUBSCRIPTIONS AND REDEMPTIONS
articles.summary: Open USD (OUSD) is now the default stablecoin for minting and redeeming Ondo's USDY on Tempo.

articles.title: ONCHAIN OPTIONS HIT A RECORD MONTH AT $170M PREMIUM
articles.summary: Onchain options saw $170.1M of premium over 30 days, $1.99B in open interest, and $1B in all-time premium.

articles.title: 10,000+ VERTICAL NEOBANKS WILL LAUNCH OVER THE NEXT DECADE
articles.summary: Neobanks are being built for narrow customer groups such as real estate agents, medical offices, immigrant communities, music artists and labels, staffing agencies, and restaurant owners.

articles.title: BTCS SELLS 27,300 ETH TO CUT AAVE DEBT 81%
articles.summary: Nasdaq-listed BTCS sold about 27,300 ETH on November 20 to repay $43.8M of Aave loans, leaving roughly $10.5M of Aave debt at about 32% loan-to-value.
